title: Vista do Rei
description: Twin crater lakes, one blue one green, split by a single isthmus below an abandoned hotel balcony. Ten minutes from the car park and the whole caldera opens up. Bring a jacket — the rim catches wind even on calm days.
region: Sete Cidades overlook, São Miguel, Azores Natural Park

title: Pico Mountain Summit Trail
description: Portugal's highest point is a volcanic cone you climb hand-over-hand on the upper pitch, ropes bolted into lava rock. Register at the base hut before sunrise starts. Clear days show every island in the chain from the crater rim.
region: Montanha do Pico, Pico Island, Azores

title: Furnas Fumarole Trail
description: Boiling mud pots ring the village and cooks bury pots of cozido stew in the ground overnight. The short loop trail smells like sulfur and lunch at the same time. Stick to marked paths — the crust is thin.

title: Caldeira do Faial Rim Walk
description: A near-perfect volcanic crater half a mile across, its floor a green tangle of laurel forest. The rim trail circles the edge in cloud that rolls in fast. Pair it with the Capelinhos lighthouse drive for the full island loop.
region: Caldeira do Faial, Faial Island, Azores

title: Ponta da Ferraria Tide Pools
description: Volcanic hot springs mix with Atlantic surf in natural rock pools at the island's western tip. Best at low tide when the pools fill with warm water instead of getting scoured by waves. Free and unfenced — read the tide chart first.
region: Ponta da Ferraria, São Miguel, Azores

title: Caldera de Taburiente Rim Trail
description: An eight-kilometer-wide erosion crater cloaked in Canary pine, with waterfalls feeding the Barranco de las Angustias below. The Lomo de las Chozas viewpoint is the easy version; the full descent is a long day. Pack more water than you think.
region: Caldera de Taburiente National Park, La Palma

title: Roque Nublo Trailhead
description: A basalt monolith sacred to the island's original Guanche people, reached by a short, steep trail from the Degollada de la Goleta car park. Sunset turns the rock and the volcanic backcountry orange in the same ten minutes. Parking fills early on weekends.

title: Masca Gorge Trailhead
description: A narrow ravine trail drops from a cliffside village to a black-sand cove, requiring a timed entry permit and roughly four hours down. Boats ferry hikers back rather than making them climb out. Flash-flood closures happen without much warning.

title: Timanfaya Fire Mountains Overlook
description: Volcanic cones from 18th-century eruptions still radiate heat a few feet below the surface, demonstrated at the visitor center with straw fires and geysers. Independent hiking is restricted, but the Ruta de los Volcanes bus loop covers the dramatic core. Book the coach slot online in summer.

title: Fogo Volcano Crater Trail
description: A village of vintners lives inside the caldera of an active volcano that last erupted in 2014, and a local guide leads the crater-rim climb from there. The wine, grown in black ash soil, is worth the detour alone. Guides are mandatory and easy to arrange in the village.
region: Chã das Caldeiras, Fogo Island, Cape Verde

title: Paul Valley Ribeira Trail
description: Terraced sugarcane and banana plots stack up a green ravine walled in by volcanic peaks, with a cobbled trail linking hillside hamlets. Local rum stills sit right along the path if you want to sample grogue mid-hike. Afternoon cloud rolls in fast on the north coast.
region: Ribeira do Paul, Santo Antão, Cape Verde

title: Cova Crater Rim Trail
description: An old volcanic crater now farmed in neat green plots, ringed by a rim trail with views down to the coast. It's a short, flat loop that pairs well with a longer Paul Valley day. Go early before the crater fills with haze.
region: Cova Crater, Santo Antão, Cape Verde

title: Pico Ruivo Summit Trail
description: Madeira's highest peak, reached by a well-built stone trail from Achada do Teixeira through cloud forest and volcanic scree. The summit hut serves coffee if the weather turns. Combine with the Pico do Areeiro ridge for the island's classic traverse.

title: Levada do Caldeirão Verde
description: An old irrigation channel trail cut into cliffside, passing through tunnels and laurel forest to a waterfall pool. Levadas like this one water the island's terraces and double as some of its best hiking paths. Bring a headlamp for the unlit tunnel sections.

title: Cabo Girão Skywalk
description: One of Europe's highest sea cliffs, with a glass-floored platform suspended 580 meters above banana terraces and the Atlantic. It's a five-minute stroll from the car park, no hiking required. Vertigo is the only real obstacle here.
region: Cabo Girão, Câmara de Lobos, Madeira

title: Piton de la Fournaise Crater Trail
description: One of the world's most active volcanoes, with a trail across the Plaine des Sables lava desert to the crater rim when activity levels allow. Check the volcano observatory's status before driving up — access closes fast during eruptions. The moonscape approach alone is worth the trip.
region: Pas de Bellecombe, Piton de la Fournaise, Reunion

title: Cirque de Mafate Traverse
description: A volcanic amphitheater with no road access at all — every one of its hamlets is reached only on foot or by helicopter. Multi-day treks link creole villages clinging to cliff ledges above the void. Gîtes along the way mean you don't need to carry a tent.
region: Marla village, Cirque de Mafate, Reunion

title: Cirque de Cilaos Rim Viewpoint
description: A thermal-spring town wedged into a second volcanic cirque, ringed by trails climbing to jagged rim peaks like Piton des Neiges. The switchback road in is a white-knuckle warm-up for the hiking. Local lentils and wine are a well-earned reward.

title: Alexandra Falls Viewpoint Trail
description: A short forest walk to a viewpoint over cascading falls and the gorge's deep green canopy, with deer sometimes visible below. It's the easiest window into Mauritius's only mountain rainforest. Combine it with the Black River Peak trail for a longer day.
region: Black River Gorges National Park, Mauritius

title: Le Morne Brabant Trailhead
description: A basalt monolith sacred as a memorial to escaped slaves, with a steep trail requiring a registered local guide past the halfway point. The summit view stretches across turquoise lagoon to the reef line. Guides can be booked same-day at the base.

title: Morne Seychellois Trail
description: Mahé's granite spine, cloaked in mist forest and endemic pitcher plants, with a ridge trail linking Trois Frères to the island's highest peak. Views drop straight to Victoria and the turquoise water beyond. Trails are quiet even in high season.
region: Morne Seychellois National Park, Mahé, Seychelles

title: Anse Lazio Beach Trail
description: A short coastal path over granite headlands leads to a beach regularly ranked among the world's best, framed by giant boulders and takamaka trees. No entry fee, just a bit of a walk or drive from the main road. Arrive early to beat the day-trip crowds from Mahé.

title: Vallée de Mai Palm Forest Trail
description: A UNESCO-listed palm forest and the only place on Earth the coco de mer grows wild, its giant double coconuts littering the trail. A modest entry fee funds the reserve. The black parrot calling overhead is endemic and endangered.
region: Vallée de Mai Nature Reserve, Praslin, Seychelles

title: Gypsy Cove Trail
description: A coastal walk just outside Stanley to a beach where Magellanic penguins burrow in the dunes, with shipwreck remains visible offshore. It's the easiest wildlife payoff on the islands, no boat required. Stick to the marked path — the area was once mined and isn't fully cleared beyond it.

title: Volunteer Point Penguin Colony
description: A remote private reserve reached by a rough overland drive across camp track, home to the islands' largest king penguin colony alongside gentoos and magellanics. Access requires booking with the landowners in advance. The white sand beach backdrop makes it feel improbably tropical.

title: Jvari Monastery Overlook
description: A sixth-century monastery perched where the Aragvi and Mtkvari rivers meet, the view that opens Georgia's national epic poem. It's a short walk from the car park to the overlook terrace. Come at golden hour when both rivers catch the light differently.

title: Jvari Pass Overlook
description: The high point of the historic road linking Tbilisi to the North Caucasus, marked by a Soviet-era mosaic monument above a sweeping glacial valley. Snow closes it well into late spring some years. Trucks and marshrutkas share the switchbacks, so drive with patience.
region: Cross Pass, Georgian Military Highway, Georgia

title: Listvyanka Baikal Shoreline
description: The easiest gateway to the world's deepest lake, with a shoreline promenade, fish market, and boat trips out onto Baikal's improbably clear water. In winter the lake freezes into blue ice slabs you can walk on. It's an easy add-on from the Trans-Siberian line through Irkutsk.

title: Circum-Baikal Railway Trail
description: A decommissioned rail line hugging Baikal's shore through dozens of hand-cut tunnels, now walked or biked rather than ridden. It was once the final gap-closing link of the Trans-Siberian route. Boats connect back to Listvyanka when the trail runs out.

title: Stolby Nature Reserve Trail
description: Towering granite pillars rise straight out of taiga forest just outside a major Trans-Siberian stop, popular with free climbers for over a century. Marked trails loop between the formations without technical gear needed. It's an easy half-day break from a long train journey.

title: Laguna de los Tres Trailhead
description: Argentina's trekking capital sits at the base of this trail to a turquoise lake beneath Mount Fitz Roy's needle spires. No permit needed, just an early start to beat the wind and clouds that roll in by midday. The town itself has zero entry fee to the whole park system.
region: El Chaltén, Los Glaciares National Park, Argentina

title: Bahía Lapataia Trail
description: The literal end of the Pan-American Highway, a quiet bay trail through lenga forest and peat bog at the southern tip of the Americas. A signpost here marks the road's terminus. Beavers, introduced decades ago, have reshaped much of the surrounding forest.
region: Tierra del Fuego National Park, Ushuaia, Argentina

title: Cerro Castillo Traverse Trailhead
description: A jagged, castle-like massif along Chile's Carretera Austral, with a multi-day traverse past turquoise tarns beneath the peak. It sees a fraction of Torres del Paine's crowds for comparable scenery. Permits and campsite reservations are required in high season.
region: Cerro Castillo National Park, Aysén, Chile

title: Dientes de Navarino Circuit
description: The southernmost trekking circuit on Earth, a five-day unmarked route through jagged peaks south of the Beagle Channel. Navigation is genuinely difficult and rescue is far away, so registration with local authorities is required. It's the real alternative for hikers who find Patagonia's main circuits too crowded.

title: Marble Caves Boat Trail
description: Wind and glacial-blue water have carved marble caverns into swirling patterns along General Carrera Lake. Small boats from Puerto Río Tranquilo run the short crossing when the lake is calm enough. Light conditions change the color of the caves dramatically through the day.
region: Capillas de Mármol, Puerto Río Tranquilo, Chile

title: Todra Gorge Trailhead
description: A narrow limestone canyon with walls rising 300 meters above a shallow river, popular with rock climbers and walkers alike. The gorge road is drivable, with trails branching off upstream into quieter side canyons. Berber villages along the approach still irrigate palm groves the old way.

title: Poon Hill Sunrise Trail
description: A pre-dawn climb above a rhododendron-forest village to a viewpoint stacked with Annapurna and Dhaulagiri's full range at sunrise. It's the classic short trek for those without time for the full Annapurna circuit. A conservation area permit and TIMS card are required at the trailhead.

title: Rohtang Pass Overlook
description: A high Himalayan pass linking the Kullu Valley to Lahaul and Spiti, with snowfields lingering well into summer even as flowers bloom below. An online permit and rotation system limits daily vehicle numbers. It's a full day trip from Manali by taxi or motorbike.
region: Rohtang Pass, Manali, Himachal Pradesh, India

title: Chadar Frozen River Trek
description: A winter trek across the frozen surface of the Zanskar River itself, the traditional route linking Zanskar villages to the outside world when mountain passes are snowbound. Guides and permits are mandatory, and ice conditions shift year to year. It's one of the most physically demanding treks still open to non-mountaineers.

title: Sandakphu Kanchenjunga Viewpoint
description: The highest point in West Bengal, offering a rare four-summit panorama including Everest, Kanchenjunga, Lhotse, and Makalu on a clear morning. The multi-day ridge trail can also be done by Land Rover jeep track. Permits from Singalila National Park are required at the entry gate.

title: Markha Valley Trek Trailhead
description: A multi-day trail through a high-desert valley past Buddhist villages and monasteries beneath 6,000-meter peaks. It crosses the Kongmaru La pass at over 5,200 meters near the end. Permits through Hemis National Park are checked at several points along the route.
region: Markha Valley, Hemis National Park, Ladakh, India

title: Simien Mountains Escarpment Trail
description: A jagged escarpment dropping thousands of feet in sheer cliffs, home to endemic gelada monkeys and Walia ibex found nowhere else. A scout and guide are required and arranged in Debark before entry. Multi-day treks link camps along the plateau rim.
region: Debark, Simien Mountains National Park, Ethiopia

title: Jomon Sugi Ancient Cedar Trail
description: A long day hike through moss-draped cedar forest to a tree over 2,000 years old, on an island so wet it inspired the forests of Princess Mononoke. Trailhead access requires an early shuttle bus from the village. Rain gear is not optional here — the island earns its reputation.

title: Pinaisara Falls Trail
description: A mix of kayaking up a mangrove river and jungle trail leads to Okinawa's tallest waterfall, deep in a subtropical island more forest than town. Guides are recommended for the river sections when tides shift. Iriomote cats, a critically endangered subspecies, live only here.

title: Cape Sukoton Trail
description: Japan's northernmost inhabited island, carpeted with alpine wildflowers at sea level thanks to its cold maritime climate, with a coastal trail to its windswept northern cape. Russia's Sakhalin coast is visible on clear days. The flower season is short, peaking in June.

title: Mount Rishiri Summit Trail
description: A near-symmetrical volcanic cone rising straight out of the Sea of Japan, visible from the ferry long before landfall. The summit trail is a full-day round trip with no huts above the treeline. Weather changes fast on an island with almost nothing to block the wind.

title: Chichijima Trail
description: A subtropical island reachable only by a 24-hour ferry from Tokyo, with jungle trails, hidden beaches, and waters where dolphins and humpback whales are common. There's no airport, which keeps the island genuinely remote for a place administratively part of Tokyo. Ferries run only a few times a month.

title: Auyuittuq Overlord Trailhead
description: A trail into a fjord-and-glacier wilderness above the Arctic Circle, passing Thor Peak's sheer granite face en route to Summit Lake. Registration with Parks Canada and a satellite messenger are required before setting out. Access to Pangnirtung itself is by plane or, in season, boat.

title: Qikiqtarjuaq Iceberg Trail
description: A small Inuit community on Broughton Island known as an iceberg gateway, with floe-edge tours by snowmobile and boat depending on season. Narwhal pass close to shore in summer months. Everything here runs on local guide knowledge — there are no marked trails.

title: Cambridge Bay Arctic Trail
description: A hub community on Victoria Island along the Northwest Passage, with tundra walking routes to Inuit historic sites and the wreck of HMS Erebus on display nearby. Wildlife includes musk ox herds visible from town. Flights connect from Yellowknife, as there's no road access.

title: Tuktoyaktuk Ice Road Overlook
description: A Inuvialuit hamlet on the Arctic Ocean, reachable by an all-season gravel highway completed in 2017 — the first road in Canada to touch the Arctic coast. Pingo ice hills dot the surrounding tundra and are a short boat trip from town. Dip a toe in the Arctic Ocean at the public beach.

title: Sirmilik National Park Gateway
description: One of the northernmost national parks in Canada, with floe-edge wildlife tours for narwhal, polar bear, and seabirds each spring. Parks Canada permits and local Inuit guides are required for backcountry travel. Bylot Island's bird cliffs within the park are a major seabird nesting site.
region: Pond Inlet, Sirmilik National Park, Nunavut

title: Lion's Head Trail
description: A spiral trail with chain-and-ladder sections circling a peak between Table Mountain and Signal Hill, popular for full-moon night hikes. Sunrise and sunset both draw crowds for the 360-degree city and ocean views. It's short enough to do before breakfast.
region: Lion's Head, Table Mountain National Park, Cape Town, South Africa

title: God's Window Viewpoint
description: A short forest trail to a viewpoint where the Drakensberg escarpment drops nearly a kilometer to the lowveld below, often through drifting cloud. It's one stop on the Panorama Route above the Kruger lowlands. Come early — mist frequently obscures the view by mid-morning.
region: Blyde River Canyon, Mpumalanga, South Africa

title: Amphitheatre Trailhead
description: A five-kilometer basalt wall forming one of the Drakensberg's most dramatic escarpments, with a chain-ladder trail climbing to the Tugela Falls plateau above. The falls rank among the world's tallest when in flow. Weather on the escarpment can turn dangerous with little warning.
region: Royal Natal National Park, Drakensberg, South Africa

title: Parque Lage Corcovado Trail
description: A jungle trail starting from a colonial-era garden climbs through Tijuca Forest to the base of Christ the Redeemer, an alternative to the train up Corcovado. It's steep, shaded, and considerably less crowded. Go with a group — solo robbery has been reported on this trail.
region: Parque Lage, Rio de Janeiro, Brazil

title: Dove Lake Circuit
description: A boardwalk and forest loop around a glacial lake mirroring Cradle Mountain's jagged dolerite profile, one of Tasmania's most photographed scenes. A shuttle bus runs from the visitor center in peak season. It also marks the start of the multi-day Overland Track.
region: Cradle Mountain-Lake St Clair National Park, Tasmania, Australia

title: Milford Track Trailhead
description: Often called the finest walk in the world, a four-day hut-to-hut trek through rainforest, over Mackinnon Pass, and down to Milford Sound. Hut bookings sell out months ahead in the Great Walks season. Sandflies at the huts are as legendary as the scenery.
region: Glade Wharf, Fiordland National Park, New Zealand

title: Tongariro Alpine Crossing Trailhead
description: A volcanic day crossing past emerald crater lakes and active steam vents, used as Mordor's backdrop in film but entirely its own place in person. Shuttle buses are required since it's a one-way point-to-point track. Weather above the treeline can turn from clear to whiteout within minutes.
region: Mangatepopo, Tongariro National Park, New Zealand

title: Routeburn Track Trailhead
description: A multi-day alpine crossing linking Mount Aspiring and Fiordland national parks over the Harris Saddle, with views across the Hollyford Valley to the Darran Mountains. Great Walk hut and campsite bookings are required in the main season. Day-trippers can still reach the Routeburn Flats and back.
region: Routeburn Flats, Mount Aspiring National Park, New Zealand

title: Besseggen Ridge Trailhead
description: A narrow glacial ridge trail with a lake of milky turquoise glacial melt on one side and deep blue on the other, considered one of Norway's classic day hikes. A boat shuttle across Lake Gjende shortens the traverse. Weather and wind on the exposed ridge can change quickly.

title: Trolltunga Trailhead
description: A rock slab jutting horizontally 700 meters above a fjord, now one of the most photographed hikes in Norway and correspondingly crowded in summer. It's a long day at roughly 27 kilometers round trip. Snow can linger on the approach well into June.

title: Kjeragbolten Trailhead
description: A boulder wedged in a crevasse a thousand meters above the fjord, where hikers pose standing on it above open air. The approach involves chain-assisted rock scrambles rather than a simple trail. It draws base jumpers as much as hikers.

title: Svartifoss Waterfall Trail
description: A short forest trail leads to a waterfall framed by dark hexagonal basalt columns that inspired the design of Reykjavik's main cathedral. It's an easy add-on to any Ring Road itinerary. The path continues further for views onto nearby glacier tongues.

title: Landmannalaugar Trailhead
description: A rhyolite mountain area streaked in red, yellow, and green, with natural hot springs to soak in after a day of hiking. It's the start or end point of the multi-day Laugavegur Trail. The mountain F-road access is only open a few months a year and requires a 4x4.

title: Fimmvörðuháls Pass Trailhead
description: A high pass trail between two glaciers linking Skógafoss waterfall to the Þórsmörk valley, crossing ground reshaped by a 2010 eruption. It's a full day of roughly 25 kilometers with real elevation gain. Weather here shifts from sun to sleet within the hour.

title: Þórsmörk Valley Trail
description: A green valley wedged between three glaciers, reachable only by river-fording super jeep or bus due to the unbridged crossings on the access road. It's a hub for several of Iceland's best multi-day treks. Rental cars without high clearance are turned back at the river.

title: Hornstrandir Nature Reserve Trail
description: An uninhabited peninsula abandoned by its last residents in the 1950s, now reachable only by boat and roamed by one of Iceland's healthiest arctic fox populations. There are no roads, shops, or rescue services inside the reserve. It's open only in the brief summer window between snow seasons.

title: Kallur Lighthouse Trail
description: A ridge trail along a narrow island to a lighthouse perched above sheer sea cliffs, one of the most photographed views in the Faroes. A short ferry from Klaksvík reaches the island. Wind on the exposed ridge can be strong enough to affect balance.

title: Drangarnir Sea Stack Viewpoint
description: A pair of dramatic sea stacks off Vágar's coast, viewable from a coastal trail across private farmland that requires a paid access permit. Boat tours offer a closer alternative for those short on time. The trail also passes the abandoned village site of Slættanes.

title: Deadvlei Clay Pan Trail
description: A white clay pan studded with 900-year-old dead camel thorn trees, ringed by some of the world's tallest red sand dunes. It's a short walk in soft sand from the 4x4 parking area. Early morning light is what every photograph of this place is chasing.

title: Dune 45 Trail
description: One of the most climbed dunes on Earth, a star dune rising 85 meters right beside the main park road, popular for sunrise ascents. No technical skill is needed, just soft-sand stamina. The ridge walk up offers views across the whole dune sea.
region: Dune 45, Sossusvlei, Namib-Naukluft National Park, Namibia

title: Spitzkoppe Trail
description: Granite peaks rising abruptly from flat desert plains, nicknamed the Matterhorn of Africa, with ancient San rock art in nearby shelters. Informal campsites sit right at the base among the boulders. Sunset and sunrise both turn the granite a deep orange-red.

title: Ala Kul Lake Trek Trailhead
description: A high alpine lake reached by a two-to-three-day trek over a 3,860-meter pass in the Tian Shan range, starting from Altyn Arashan hot springs. Weather above the pass can turn to snow even in summer. It's one of Central Asia's most rewarding multi-day treks for the effort involved.

title: Karakul Lake Viewpoint
description: A high-altitude lake formed by an ancient meteorite impact, sitting at nearly 4,000 meters along the Pamir Highway near the Kyrgyz border. GBAO permits are required for the entire region. The thin air and total remoteness make it feel like a different planet from the rest of Tajikistan.

title: Mount Bromo Viewpoint Trail
description: An active volcano rising out of a vast sea of volcanic sand, with a short climb to the crater rim after a jeep or horseback approach across the caldera floor. Sunrise from Mount Penanjakan is the classic photo stop before the crossing. Sulfur fumes are strong near the rim itself.
region: Mount Bromo, Bromo Tengger Semeru National Park, Java, Indonesia

title: Kawah Ijen Crater Trail
description: A pre-dawn climb rewarded by electric-blue sulfur flames burning at the crater's edge, visible only in full darkness before sunrise. Miners still carry sulfur blocks out by hand along the same trail. A gas mask is worth renting at the base for the fumes near the rim.

title: Mount Rinjani Summit Trail
description: Indonesia's second-highest volcano, with a multi-day trek to a crater lake and hot springs before the final steep summit push for sunrise. Porters and guides are mandatory and easily arranged in Senaru or Sembalun. The trail was rebuilt after 2018 earthquake damage closed it for a time.

title: Batad Rice Terraces Trail
description: A 2,000-year-old amphitheater of hand-carved rice terraces reachable only on foot from the nearest road, with a village built directly into the terraced slope. A local guide is recommended given the maze of paths. A waterfall trek continues beyond the main viewpoint for those with an extra hour.

title: Cat Ba National Park Trail
description: Limestone karst forest trails climb to a viewing tower overlooking Lan Ha Bay's scattered islands, a quieter alternative to the boat-choked core of Halong Bay. The endangered Cat Ba langur survives only on this island. Kayak add-ons from nearby villages extend the day onto the water.
region: Cat Ba National Park, Cat Ba Island, Vietnam

title: Jebel Umm ad Dami Trail
description: Jordan's highest peak, a desert summit trail through Wadi Rum's red sandstone country to a viewpoint reaching into Saudi Arabia. A Bedouin guide is required to arrange the 4x4 approach and final climb. Overnight desert camps in the valley make a natural base.

title: Dana Biosphere Reserve Trail
description: A trail dropping from a 15th-century stone village down through desert canyon to the Feynan eco-lodge, crossing several ecological zones along the way. It's one of Jordan's oldest protected areas and a haven for ibex and rare birds. Guides can be arranged through the village guesthouse.

title: Samaria Gorge Trail
description: One of Europe's longest canyon hikes, a 16-kilometer descent through a national park to the Libyan Sea, passing the narrow Iron Gates where the walls close to a few meters apart. The gorge closes entirely outside the May–October season. A ferry back from Agia Roumeli is the standard exit.
region: Samaria Gorge National Park, Crete, Greece

title: Vikos Gorge Trail
description: Listed by Guinness as the world's deepest gorge relative to its width, with stone-village trailheads on either rim connected by an old shepherd's path. Zagori's stone-built villages and bridges make a striking approach. It sees a fraction of Samaria's crowds despite comparable drama.

title: Sentiero Azzurro Trailhead
description: The Blue Trail links five cliffside fishing villages along Italy's Ligurian coast, with vineyard terraces stacked above turquoise water. A park card covers trail access and includes the connecting train between villages. Sections close periodically after landslides, so check status before setting out.
region: Cinque Terre National Park, Liguria, Italy

title: Tre Cime di Lavaredo Loop Trail
description: A loop trail circling three iconic limestone towers that were a front line in World War One, with abandoned trench networks still visible along the route. Rifugio Locatelli marks the halfway point for a coffee break. Parking at the trailhead fills before 9am in summer.
region: Tre Cime di Lavaredo, Dolomites, Italy

title: GR20 Northern Trailhead
description: Widely rated one of Europe's toughest long-distance trails, a two-week traverse of Corsica's granite spine with chains and cables on its most exposed sections. Refuges along the route require booking well ahead in July and August. Many hikers underestimate it and bail within the first three days.

title: Cares Gorge Trail
description: A cliffside path carved into limestone gorge walls, originally built for hydroelectric maintenance and now one of Spain's most popular day hikes. It links the villages of Caín and Poncebos over about twelve kilometers. Tunnels and narrow ledges along the way have no real barriers.
region: Ruta del Cares, Picos de Europa National Park, Spain

title: Sirimon Route Trailhead
description: The driest and often preferred approach to Mount Kenya's trekking peaks, climbing through moorland studded with giant lobelia to Point Lenana. Park fees and a registered guide are required at the gate. Altitude sickness is a real risk given the pace most visitors attempt.
region: Mount Kenya National Park, Sirimon Gate, Kenya

title: Rwenzori Central Circuit Trailhead
description: The fabled Mountains of the Moon, a multi-day trek through bog, bamboo, and glacier remnants near the equator, among the muddiest and most physically demanding treks in Africa. Porters and guides are mandatory through the park authority. Rwenzori's equatorial glaciers are retreating fast, so this is a shrinking window.

title: Zomba Plateau Trail
description: A pine-forested plateau above Malawi's old colonial capital, with trails to waterfalls and a viewpoint over Lake Malawi on clear days. Horseback tours run from the plateau's forestry lodge. It's a cooler retreat from the heat of the Rift Valley floor below.

title: Bwindi Gorilla Trek Trailhead
description: Dense montane rainforest home to roughly half the world's remaining mountain gorillas, tracked on foot with rangers through terrain that can take anywhere from one to eight hours to find a habituated family. Permits are limited and should be booked months ahead. The forest's density makes it feel far older than its name suggests.

title: Ausangate Trek Trailhead
description: A multi-day circuit around a sacred glaciated peak, passing the striped Vinicunca Rainbow Mountain and turquoise glacial lakes above 4,500 meters. Community-run campsites charge small access fees along the route. Altitude here is more demanding than most of the Inca Trail.

title: Laguna 69 Trail
description: A day hike through the Cordillera Blanca to a glacial lake beneath Nevado Chacraraju's twin ice spires, one of the range's most rewarded short treks. Park entry fees are collected at the gate. The final push above 4,500 meters is steep enough to slow most visitors.

title: Furnas Lake Loop Trail
description: A flat forest loop around a crater lake dotted with hydrangeas and hidden fumarole vents at the water's edge. It's an easy counterpart to the steeper Sete Cidades hikes elsewhere on the island. Tea plantations sit just up the road for an easy add-on stop.

title: Anse Source d'Argent Trail
description: Granite boulders the size of houses frame one of the most photographed beaches on Earth, reached by a short walk or bike ride from La Digue's main village. Ox-carts and bicycles are still the island's main transport. Low tide exposes tidepools worth exploring around the boulders.

title: Ulan-Ude Ivolginsky Datsan Trail
description: Siberia's main Buddhist monastery complex sits on the steppe outside a Trans-Siberian stop near Lake Baikal, with a short pilgrim path circling its temples and stupas. It's an easy half-day detour by minibus from Ulan-Ude. The datsan remains an active center of Buryat Buddhist practice.

title: Bahía Rosas Beach Trail
description: A gentler slice of the Patagonian Atlantic coast, with soft cliffside paths above tide pools and sea lion haul-outs near a small resort town. It's a good low-effort stop for travelers heading south toward the harder trekking in Chubut and Santa Cruz. Whale-watching season peaks from June through December nearby at Puerto Madryn.
region: Las Grutas coastal trail, Patagonia, Argentina

title: Anse Georgette Trail
description: A quieter cove trail past the Constance Lemuria resort golf course, ending at a beach with almost no development along its curve. It's reachable on foot or by a short paid resort shuttle, and open to the public via the coastal path. Fewer visitors make it than the more famous Anse Lazio just over the ridge.
